props.title: The Wedding Date
props.initialSlug: When love's the target, she's the date.

sections.content: The Wedding Date (2005) follows the familiar romantic comedy template established by Pretty Woman (1990), flipping the gender dynamics of hiring an escort. Debra Messing plays Kat, who hires male escort Nick (Dermot Mulroney) to pose as her date at her sister's wedding. While the film received mixed reviews, it taps into the rich tradition of wedding-centered romantic comedies like Four Weddings and a Funeral (1994) and My Best Friend's Wedding (1997), using the heightened emotions and social pressures of wedding celebrations to drive character development and romantic tension.

sections.content: The "hired date" premise gained popularity in the 1990s and 2000s, seen in films like Can't Buy Me Love (1987) and Drive Me Crazy (1999). These plots explore themes of authenticity versus pretense in relationships, often revealing how "fake" arrangements lead to genuine connections. The Wedding Date adds complexity by making the male lead the escort, challenging gender expectations while maintaining the genre's core fantasy of finding love in unexpected places.

The film's London setting follows a trend of American romantic comedies using British locations and supporting casts to add sophistication and charm, similar to What a Girl Wants (2003) and Bridget Jones's Diary (2001). This Anglo-American fusion creates a heightened sense of romance and escapism while playing with cultural differences for both comedy and dramatic effect. sections.content: Wedding-themed romantic comedies evolved significantly from the screwball era of The Philadelphia Story (1940) to modern interpretations like 27 Dresses (2008). These films increasingly focused on examining the wedding industry itself and the social pressures surrounding marriage, rather than just using weddings as a backdrop. The Wedding Date bridges this transition, maintaining traditional romantic elements while acknowledging the commodification of romance through Nick's profession.
